title: Integrating Techno-Economic Modeling and Machine Learning for Green Hydrogen Development: Comparative Insights from Costa Rica and the UK
content: Green hydrogen is increasingly recognized as a pivotal solution for decarbonizing energy systems, yet its economic viability varies widely across national contexts. This study introduces an integrated, multi-scale framework that combines high-resolution spatial renewable resource mapping, deterministic techno-economic modeling, Monte Carlo financial simulations, and machine learning–accelerated forecasting to assess green hydrogen development in Costa Rica and the United Kingdom. Leveraging ensemble algorithms—LightGBM, Random Forest, and XGBoost—the framework predicts Levelized Cost of Hydrogen (LCOH) and Net Present Value (NPV) trajectories under cost, resource, and policy uncertainty. Machine learning models achieved high predictive accuracy—R² = 0.990 (PEM) in the United Kingdom and R² = 0.992 (SOEC) in Costa Rica—while probabilistic simulations revealed that large-scale projects in the UK, supported by structured incentives, deliver robust NPVs. In contrast, Costa Rica’s smaller-scale initiatives face profitability constraints despite abundant renewables, underscoring the need for scale-sensitive financial mechanisms. Sensitivity analysis identifies project scale, electricity pricing, and policy stacking as dominant cost drivers. The study further highlights opportunities for bilateral collaboration, including leveraging Guanacaste’s wind resources through joint offshore hydrogen projects integrating UK expertise. By advancing a transferable and interpretable modeling approach, this research provides a generalizable toolset for supporting context-sensitive green hydrogen deployment across diverse geopolitical settings.
